summary: NebulaRetail production: streaming resets during peak causing partial duplicated completions and billing delta — customer escalated, require post-incident reconciliation
description: Issue summary: During NebulaRetail's evening peak (approx 18:45-19:30 PST on 2026-03-05) customers observed intermittent streaming resets which produced partial duplicated completions for a subset of chat sessions. The duplicated tokens resulted in an observable delta on NebulaRetail invoices and triggered an enterprise-level escalation. Impact: ~0.7% of NebulaRetail's requests in us-west-2 experienced either truncated streaming followed by replayed tokens or duplicate completions, resulting in an estimated billing delta of ~12k USD for the 24-hour window and several customer-facing user errors (duplicated order confirmations). Environment: production, us-west-2, routed through primary api-gateway cluster agw-usw2-1. Timeline: 18:42 detection by NebulaWebhook alert; 18:46 auto-alert triggered in Redwood SRE dashboard (elevated 5xx and streaming disconnects); 18:55 Support engaged customer and opened ticket; 19:10 SRE rolled emergency kernel fallback and disabled the aggressive prefix-replay optimization; 19:35 streaming stability returned to baseline. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send long-running streaming chat sessions at high concurrency with pinned model redwood-large-rlhf-v2; 2) Simulate abrupt connection resets mid-stream; 3) Observe service replays and duplicate completions in 1-2% of sessions. Observed logs: repeated KVCACHE_INVALIDATION errors on serving node rnode-14, partial stream offsets returned in EnvelopeStreamResponse, and billing-collector recorded double-counts for ephemeral token windows. Detection and escalation: NebulaRetail filed an enterprise escalation after noticing duplicate order confirmations tied to completion IDs; account executive joined the incident bridge and requested invoice reconciliation and an RCA.
comments: Maya Patel (2026-03-05 19:01 UTC): Initial triage — elevated streaming disconnect rate and duplicate completions reported by NebulaRetail. Creating ticket and engaging SRE. Notified #incidents.

Rishi Menon, SRE (2026-03-05 19:12 UTC): Observed KVCACHE_INVALIDATION spikes on rnode-12/14 coincident with scheduler rebalances. Starting kernel fallback to last-known-good build v1.8.2-rc and disabling prefix-replay optimization as mitigation.

Liam O'Connor (2026-03-05 19:20 UTC): Applied emergency rollback on serving-runtime (PR/1882) — streaming resets dropped to baseline within 15 minutes. Notifying NebulaRetail of mitigation and collecting request IDs for billing reconciliation.

Customer rep — Julie Park, NebulaRetail (2026-03-05 19:30 UTC): Thanks for quick response. We saw duplicate order notifications for about 60 sessions. Customer needs invoice adjustments and a full RCA for compliance audit.

Finance Ops — Elena Ruiz (2026-03-06 10:32 UTC): Receiving token accounting dump from billing-collector. Starting reconciliation job against NebulaRetail usage window. Estimated delta ~12k USD pending verification.

Rishi Menon (2026-03-07 14:05 UTC): Root cause hypothesis: a race between session affinity handoff during an autoscaler shrink and aggressive prefix-replay optimization caused partial replays and duplicate token accounting. Collecting traces and KV cache dumps for final RCA.
Liam O'Connor (2026-03-12 09:10 UTC): RCA complete. Preparing runbook updates and customer-facing post-incident summary. Scheduling canary for config change in staging on 2026-03-15.
Julie Park, NebulaRetail (2026-03-13 16:45 UTC): Confirmed NebulaRetail received credit note for discrepancy. Requesting runbook item to avoid recurrence during Black Friday-style peaks.
investigation_notes: Findings: 1) Scheduler performed a rapid pod shrink (autoscaler decision) while several long-lived streaming sessions used prefix-replay optimization. 2) During handoff, K/V cache entries for in-flight sessions became transiently inconsistent; the serving-runtime reissued suffix generation leading to duplicate completions for a subset of sessions. 3) Billing-collector had a windowed deduplication heuristic that failed to correlate the replayed tokens when the completion IDs were regenerated, causing double-counting. Evidence: node traces (rnode-12/14), KV cache snapshots, and billing-collector logs showing near-duplicate token batches. Confidence: High.
root_cause: Race between autoscaler-induced serving node handoff and aggressive prefix-replay optimization that allowed replayed token fragments to be treated as new tokens by billing pipeline's deduplication window.
resolution: Short-term: emergency rollback to serving-runtime v1.8.2 (disabled prefix-replay optimization) and patched billing-collector dedupe window to correlate on completion_id+session_signature. Long-term: deploy safer handoff path with session-affinity drain and KV atomicity guarantees, update autoscaler hysteresis for streaming-heavy customers. Completed: mitigation rolled out at 2026-03-05 19:10 UTC; billing credit issued to NebulaRetail on 2026-03-13.
follow_up_actions: Create and publish new runbook section: 'streaming handoff and autoscaler shrink' (owner: Serving Runtime team) — due 2026-03-20.
Add an automated check in CI for prefix-replay + autoscaler shrink scenario using the infrasim harness (owner: QA) — due 2026-04-01.
Implement a production-grade session-affinity drain mechanism to avoid mid-stream handoffs (owner: Scheduler) — target 2026-04-15.
Enhance billing-collector deduplication to use completion_id+session_signature and extend telemetry retention for post-incident audits (owner: Billing) — due 2026-03-30.
Customer-facing postmortem and SLA credit note delivered to NebulaRetail; schedule follow-up sync to review runbook changes on 2026-03-22 (owner: Support).
Track any residual invoice disputes via INT finance ticket and close after reconciliation (owner: Finance Ops) — ticket INT-83452.
notes_for_sales_cs: Customer concerned about recurrence ahead of their Q2 promotion. Recommend outreach from AE and Solutions team to walk through runbook changes and schedule a technical review. Offer two months of increased monitoring at no cost as a gesture of goodwill.
postincident_status: Runbook items created and assigned; staging canary scheduled; billing reconciliation completed and credit issued; customer follow-up meeting booked for 2026-03-22.
